questions.q: What is the zero of the linear polynomial \(p(x) = 3x - 12\)?
questions.a: The zero is \(x = 4\). A wrong answer like \(x = -4\) reveals the student incorrectly solved \(3x - 12 = 0\) as \(3x = -12\) (sign error when transposing). A wrong answer like \(x = 12/3 = 4\) but written as \(x = 3/12\) reveals confusion about the formula \(x = -b/a\) — they might have used \(b/a\) instead of \(-b/a\) or swapped numerator and denominator.

questions.q: The graph of \(y = 2x + 6\) cuts the x-axis at point A. Without drawing the graph, write the coordinates of A and explain why the x-coordinate of A is the zero of the polynomial \(2x + 6\).
questions.a: Coordinates of A are \((-3, 0)\). The x-coordinate is \(-3\) because on the x-axis \(y = 0\), so we solve \(2x + 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -3\). This value makes the polynomial zero, hence it is the zero. A wrong answer like \((0, -3)\) reveals the student confuses x-intercept with y-intercept. An answer giving only \(x = -3\) without the coordinate pair reveals they don't connect the algebraic zero to the geometric point on the graph.

questions.q: A linear polynomial \(p(x) = kx - 15\) has zero \(x = 5\). Find the value of \(k\). Then write the polynomial and state its x-intercept.
questions.a: Given zero \(x = 5\), so \(p(5) = 0 \Rightarrow k(5) - 15 = 0 \Rightarrow 5k = 15 \Rightarrow k = 3\). Polynomial: \(p(x) = 3x - 15\). X-intercept: \((5, 0)\). A wrong answer like \(k = -3\) reveals the student set \(k(5) + 15 = 0\) (sign error on constant term). A wrong answer giving x-intercept as \((0, 5)\) reveals confusion between x-intercept and y-intercept.

questions.q: Compare the zeros and x-intercepts of the two linear polynomials: \(p_1(x) = 2x + 4\) and \(p_2(x) = -2x - 4\). What do you observe about their graphs?
questions.a: Zero of \(p_1\): \(2x + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2\), x-intercept \((-2, 0)\). Zero of \(p_2\): \(-2x - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow -2x = 4 \Rightarrow x = -2\), x-intercept \((-2, 0)\). Both have the same zero and same x-intercept. The graphs are different lines (slopes 2 and -2) but they intersect the x-axis at the same point. A wrong answer claiming different zeros reveals sign errors in solving \(-2x - 4 = 0\). A student saying the graphs are the same line reveals they don't understand that different slopes give different lines even if they share an x-intercept.

questions.q: A student solves for the zero of \(p(x) = 4 - 2x\) as follows: \(4 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow -2x = -4 \Rightarrow x = -2\). Identify the error and give the correct zero.
questions.a: The error is in the last step: \(-2x = -4 \Rightarrow x = \frac{-4}{-2} = 2\), not \(-2\). The student divided \(-4\) by \(-2\) and got \(-2\) (sign error: negative divided by negative is positive). Correct zero is \(x = 2\). X-intercept is \((2, 0)\). A wrong answer that says the error is in the first step reveals the student doesn't recognize the sign mistake in division. A student who gives correct zero but cannot explain the error lacks metacognitive awareness of sign rules.

questions.q: Create a real-life situation (Indian context) that can be modeled by a linear polynomial \(p(x) = ax + b\) where \(a < 0\) and \(b > 0\). State what the zero represents in your situation and find the zero if \(a = -20\) and \(b = 500\).
questions.a: Example: A water tank has 500 litres and leaks at 20 litres per hour. Amount left after \(x\) hours: \(y = 500 - 20x\). Here \(a = -20\), \(b = 500\). Zero: \(500 - 20x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 25\) hours. The zero represents the time when the tank becomes empty. A poor answer might give a situation with \(a > 0\) (e.g., saving money) showing they don't understand the condition \(a < 0\). Or they might find zero as \(x = -25\) (sign error) showing algebraic weakness. A good answer includes correct context, correct interpretation of zero, and correct calculation.
